clue.text: Man in van retreats, losing a point. He has the remedy

indicators.note: losing says a letter drops out of the reversed word for the van's man
a man who retreats goes backwards, so the word for the van's man is read right to left

parts.note: a guard rides in the guard's van of a train
the gist is the main point of something

explanation.surface: A delivery man backs his van away, while someone with a cure waits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' reverses the van man (a railway guard, who rode in the guard's van), and 'losing' drops the letter A that the clue names.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist, the old word being chemist's shopkeeper, keeps medicines and so has the cure.

clue.text: Assimilate the laws of Justinian

definitions.meaning: the Roman law compilation ordered by the emperor Justinian

explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take in thoroughly; also the name of Justinian's summary of Roman law, the Pandects.

clue.text: Stormy variation of a French Ruy Lopez opening

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: a chess variation, here the letters taking a different order
opening means only the first letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: A stormy chess game in which a French player tries a variation of the Ruy Lopez opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ruy Lopez is a chess opening; 'variation of' shuffles UN, RUY and L, the first letter from 'opening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly, wild and disorderly, describes stormy behaviour.

clue.text: One making report on some yarn that's explosive

parts.note: a gun makes a report, a loud bang
cotton is a yarn

explanation.surface: A storyteller reports on a yarn that turns out to be explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' is a bang, not a news story, and 'yarn' is thread, not a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly flammable nitrocellulose used as a blasting agent.

clue.text: No fourth-dimensional displacement with such equations?

definitions.text: No fourth-dimensional displacement with such equations?

parts.words: No fourth-dimensional displacement with such equations?
parts.note: events not shifted at all along time, the fourth dimension, which also names a set of equations solved together

explanation.definitionFit: Happening at the same moment, with no shift in time; such equations are solved together.

clue.text: Gay, you and me? Some grounds for this

parts.note: camp means exaggeratedly effeminate, an old sense of gay
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A coy question about whether two people are gay, with some reason to ask.
explanation.definitionFit: A college's site, its buildings and lawns, is its premises or grounds.

clue.text: Like decks when the sea was high, it appears

indicators.note: it appears says the answer shows itself inside the words just before

explanation.surface: A sailor's memory of decks swamped when the sea ran high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it appears' signals letters showing inside 'sea was high'; the sailing picture hides the run across all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Decks swept by heavy seas are flooded with water.

clue.text: USA's most forceful figure

parts.note: the five-sided building that houses US military power

explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided figure, and the name of the US Defense Department's five-sided headquarters.

clue.text: " That inward eye which is the bliss of" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: " That inward eye which is the bliss of" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: " That inward eye which is the bliss of" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the missing word completing a famous line from Wordsworth's poem on daffodils

explanation.definitionFit: Being alone, which the poet says lets him recall the daffodils with that inward eye.

clue.text: East in trouble mooring Indian Chief

indicators.note: in places the compass letter inside the jumbled letters
letters in trouble are disturbed and thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A ship in difficulty at its berth on the eastern side, with a tribal leader watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges MOORING into GRONIMO and 'in' puts E inside after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache leader famed for resisting US forces in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Boy sent back out of the Navy — 'e's a weed

indicators.note: out of here means the reversed boy is placed on the outside of the remaining letters
sent back means the word for the boy is read in reverse

parts.note: a lad is a boy
RN is the Royal Navy
the Cockney 'e, with its dropped h, stands for the letter E

explanation.surface: A Cockney sailor's mate is discharged from the Navy and dismissed as a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'e's is Cockney for he's, which the setter uses for its E; 'out of' wraps the reversed boy round the Navy and that E.
explanation.definitionFit: Darnel is a ryegrass that grows as a weed among cereal crops.

clue.text: Quietly licentious revel with the Virgin Queen — good show!

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
an orgy is a wild debauched party
and means with, together with
Bess was the nickname of Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen

explanation.surface: A quiet debauched party with Elizabeth I, a good show indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth I, England's unmarried queen, was called Good Queen Bess.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's folk opera is a celebrated stage show.

clue.text: A discharge therefore without a meal-ticket

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for therefore surrounds the rest

parts.note: so means therefore
LV is a luncheon voucher, a British meal ticket given by employers

explanation.surface: Someone is discharged and so loses their meal ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old sense of outside. The meal-ticket is a Luncheon Voucher, once a common British workplace perk.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley of gunfire released at once is a discharge of guns.

clue.text: One brave as a supporter of the royal arms

definitions.text: One brave as a supporter of the royal arms

parts.words: One brave as a supporter of the royal arms
parts.note: a courageous person likened to the big cat that holds up one side of the royal coat of arms

explanation.definitionFit: Richard I was called this for his courage, likening him to the heraldic beast of the royal shield.

clue.text: Odd part of ship to deposit money in, or a choker

indicators.note: in places the money abbreviation inside the word for odd

parts.note: strange means odd
L stands for pound, the British money unit, from Latin libra
the hold is the cargo space of a ship

explanation.surface: An odd place aboard ship to stash your cash, or perhaps something worn round the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the old abbreviation for a pound, the British unit of money; 'in' puts it into STRANGE before HOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip round the throat chokes the opponent.

clue.text: Order to " Get in lane " is a bloomer

indicators.note: an order to reshape these letters, which are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A driving instruction to get in lane turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' means a flower here, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet briar, a wild rose, is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Revolutionary theatre

definitions.meaning: the London ... Theatre famous for its revues

explanation.definitionFit: Its sails turn round; also the Windmill, a London theatre that never closed in the Blitz.

clue.text: What you give a creditor in glasses? Plausible

indicators.note: in places the debt note inside the word for glasses

parts.note: specs are spectacles
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A plausible-sounding question about handing a creditor something over drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially credible but actually wrong.

clue.text: So insubstantial doesn't bear thinking about?

definitions.meaning: too light to weigh, without bulk

explanation.surface: Something so flimsy that it is better not to think about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally unweighable, from Latin pondus, weight, it means both too slight to weigh and impossible to assess by thought.

clue.text: I go into log-chopping, or a job at the Palais

indicators.note: into places the first two words inside the jumbled letters
chopping up the word log breaks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between chopping logs and a job at a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log-chopping' looks like woodwork but means LOG cut up. The Palais was the typical British dance hall, where men could be hired as dancing partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A man paid to partner women at dances, as at the Palais de Danse.

clue.text: Shut up, as writers did

definitions.meaning: confined in a pen or enclosure

explanation.definitionFit: Shut in an enclosure, and also written down, as authors do.

clue.text: Dog after a badger, or (unkindly) a sausage

definitions.meaning: a hound bred in Germany to hunt badgers
the long low breed is nicknamed the sausage dog

explanation.surface: A dog chasing a badger, or unkindly called a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: The German name means badger hound, and the long-bodied breed is jokingly called a sausage dog.

clue.text: Second wood-joiner is the go-slow type

parts.note: a nail fastens pieces of wood together

explanation.surface: A second carpenter is accused of working to rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden mollusc is proverbially slow.

clue.text: Simple as a classical four in one, nothing less

indicators.note: in places the Roman numeral piece inside the shortened word
less means the zero letter is taken away from the word one

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
O is nothing, zero
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something plain, like the classical figure four counted as one and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' takes O out of 'one'; a classical four is in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple in the sense of artless and unworldly.

clue.text: Met men knowing this line! not prohibitive

parts.note: taken as written
O as nought, zero, here reading as no
a bar is something that prohibits

explanation.surface: Weathermen insist that this line is no barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the line 'is not prohibitive', that is 'is no bar': IS, O for no, and BAR. The Met men are the British Meteorological Office forecasters.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a weather chart joining places of equal pressure, familiar to forecasters.

clue.text: Big bottle for John Anderson so called

definitions.text: Big bottle for John Anderson so called

parts.words: Big bottle for John Anderson so called
parts.note: a large wicker-covered bottle; Burns's song addresses John Anderson as 'my jo, John', a phrase that sounds much like the bottle's name

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns's song 'John Anderson, my jo' calls him 'my jo, John', jo being Scots for sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A large narrow-necked bottle in a wicker case, whose name reads as half a John.

clue.text: How a zebra's head appears, literally

definitions.text: How a zebra's head appears, literally

parts.words: How a zebra's head appears, literally
parts.note: the head of the word zebra is the letter Z, which comes at the end of the alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: Finally: the letter Z stands at the end of the alphabet.

clue.text: A body-builder sometimes — a heavenly body!

parts.note: anabolic steroids are sometimes taken by body-builders

explanation.surface: A muscle man, admired as a heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun is a celestial body.
